work_summary: turbo.json type-check/test:unit/dev depended on a task name (build:types) only 2/94 packages implement, silently skipping real builds of dependencies before type-checking anything importing them -- fixed to depend on ^build

Fixing that surfaced real breakage across ~10 packages: ui-consolidated had a dead pnpm.overrides pin (pnpm 10 moved that config to pnpm-workspace.yaml) leaving @types/react on stale 18.3.28 while 33+ packages had moved to React 19 (root cause of 1280 errors), plus 121 stale compiled .js files committed into src/, a broken package export map, an accidental type-only re-export of a real class in a2a-core, and more

feature-tracker, claude-skills, integration-tests, api-gateway, and the frontend app each had smaller real bugs (declared type-output path mismatch, missing /index.js suffixes on directory imports, a JSDoc comment whose glob pattern contained a literal star-slash that prematurely closed the comment, an undeclared this.logger, dead imports, a name/label field collision, a broken lazy route)
Result: pnpm run type-check is 100% clean across the entire monorepo (commit 2fe90b3e20)

With real test execution restored, mcp-core ran for the first time in a long while and surfaced genuine production bugs: a Promise race in ConnectionManager where the connect() timeout handler called ws.close() before rejecting (close() synchronously fires onclose, which settled the promise first with the wrong message); onerror discarded the real underlying error message; an intentional connection.close() triggered unwanted auto-reconnect instead of being distinguished from an unexpected drop; MCPErrorHandler emitted a plain error event on an EventEmitter subclass, which Node treats as fatal when unlistened, silently breaking every handleError() call (renamed to errorHandled); a classic retryPolicy.jitter

default bug where an intentional jitter:0 fell back to the 10% default; three non-functional placeholder recovery strategies were silently shadowing real ones; two timing bugs used Date.now() 1ms resolution for fast operations (switched to performance.now())

Also fixed test-only bugs: mock WebSockets racing their own auto-success timer against failure simulation, and an entire test file whose mocks used Node EventEmitter style while the real code expects the browser onopen/onclose property API (was hanging 11+ minutes)
Result: mcp-core is now 719/719 tests passing, verified in isolation (commit 13806d3f59). Both commits pushed to origin/main.
